falsification: H-C15-1: a magma with growing but sub-geometric width. H-C15-2: a bounded-width magma outside the three classes or a semigroup/affine magma with unbounded width. H-C15-3: a surjective non-permutive table or a non-surjective permutive one.

history.new: H-C15-1 (bold, inventor): no intermediate growth - the streaming width lambda(t) (the smaller of the forward and backward ordered-BDD widths of F_t) is either bounded or grows geometrically. H-C15-2 (bold, inventor): bounded streaming width holds exactly for semigroups, affine magmas x*y = ax + by + c over Z_3, and magmas whose light cone depends on at most two cells. H-C15-3 (explorer): the automaton is surjective on bi-infinite rows iff the table has all rows or all columns permutations (permutive).

methodology: Canonical representatives by minimum code over the 12 (anti-)relabellings; for each: algebraic properties, essential variables and widths of F_t (t <= 9), nilpotency, pair-graph surjectivity and injectivity, functional-graph statistics of the global map on cyclic rows.
question: For all 1734 magmas of order 3 up to isomorphism and anti-isomorphism: how complex are the t-step local maps of c'_i = c_i * c_{i+1}, which automata are surjective, and how do they behave on cyclic rows?
